notes.summary: Direction questions trace a walk or a set of turns and ask for the final direction or the shortest distance from the start. Some use the sun's shadow, and some place several points relative to each other. SSC asks about 1 question in Tier 1 and Tier 2. Draw the path as you read; it takes seconds and prevents almost every error.

concepts.title: The compass
concepts.body:
On paper, North is up, South is down, East is right and West is left. Between them are North-East (NE), South-East (SE), South-West (SW) and North-West (NW).
Opposites: N–S, E–W, NE–SW, NW–SE.
Each step around the compass from N to NE to E is 45°. A full turn is 360°.

concepts.title: Left and right turns
concepts.body:
A right turn is 90° clockwise; a left turn is 90° anticlockwise. What is "right" depends on which way the person is facing:
FacingRight turnLeft turnAbout turn
NorthEastWestSouth
EastSouthNorthWest
SouthWestEastNorth
WestNorthSouthEast
Easy check: when facing South, your right hand points West, the opposite of when facing North.

concepts.title: Turning by angles: add up the turns
concepts.body:
For many turns, do not track each one. Count clockwise turns as + and anticlockwise turns as −, add them, and turn once by the total.
Example: facing SE, turns of 135° clockwise, 90° anticlockwise, 45° clockwise and 135° anticlockwise.
Total = +135 − 90 + 45 − 135 = −45, so a single 45° anticlockwise turn. From SE, 45° anticlockwise is East.
If the total is more than 360°, subtract 360°. If you are asked for the starting direction, reverse the total and apply it to the final direction.

concepts.title: Shortest distance: net movement and Pythagoras
concepts.body:
1. Add all North moves and subtract all South moves: the net North-South distance.
  2. Add all East moves and subtract all West moves: the net East-West distance.
  3. If one of them is zero, the other is the answer.
  4. Otherwise, shortest distance = √(NS² + EW²).
Triples worth knowing (a, b, hypotenuse): 3-4-5, 6-8-10, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25, 9-12-15, 20-21-29, and their multiples (30-40-50, 200-210-290).

concepts.title: Which direction is the end point?
concepts.body:
Combine the two net moves: net North and net East means the end point is North-East of the start; net South and net West means South-West, and so on. "Exactly NE" needs equal moves; SSC options still say NE whenever both are North and East.
Watch the wording. "Direction of the house from me" and "direction of me from the house" are opposites. If the bank is South-East of the office, the office is North-West of the bank.

concepts.title: Shadows and the sun
concepts.body:
The sun rises in the East and sets in the West. A shadow always falls on the side away from the sun.
TimeSunShadow falls towards
Morning (after sunrise)EastWest
Evening (before sunset)WestEast
NoonOverheadAlmost no shadow
Morning: shadow to your left means you face North; to your right means South; in front means West; behind means East.
Evening: shadow to your left means you face South; to your right means North; in front means East; behind means West.

concepts.title: Placing points on a grid
concepts.body:
For questions with many points (houses, trees, people), put the first point at the centre (0, 0). North adds to the up value, East adds to the right value. Example: A is 30 m north of E, so A = (0, 30) when E = (0, 0). F is 50 m east of A, so F = (50, 30).
When symbols are used ("P $ Q means P is north of Q"), write the meaning of each symbol first, then place the points the same way.

concepts.title: Tricky starting points
concepts.body:
• "Exits from the back door of a north-facing house" means the person walks South at first.
  • "Walks towards the sun in the morning" means walking East.
  • "Turns back" or "about turn" is 180°.
  • If the first direction is not given ("walks X m"), describe the walk with letters, then use the final direction given in the question to fix the start.

varieties.name: Facing direction after turns
varieties.how: Count clockwise turns as + and anticlockwise as −. Add them and make one turn by the total from the starting direction.

example.q: Reeta faces South-East. She turns 135° clockwise, then 90° anticlockwise, then 45° clockwise, then 135° anticlockwise. Which way does she face now?
steps: So she turns 45° anticlockwise in all.

varieties.name: Distance and direction from start
varieties.how: Draw the walk. Find the net North-South and East-West distances, then use Pythagoras. Combine the two net directions for the final direction.

example.q: Shweta walks 150 m South, turns right and walks 80 m, turns left and walks 60 m, then turns left and walks 280 m to reach a bank. How far and in which direction is the bank from her office?
steps: Facing South, a right turn is West: 80 m West. Then left (South): 60 m South. Then left (East): 280 m East.
Net South = 150 + 60 = 210 m. Net East = 280 − 80 = 200 m.

varieties.name: Shadow questions
varieties.how: Fix where the sun is (East in the morning, West in the evening). The shadow points the other way. Then find which way the person faces so that the shadow is on the stated side.

example.q: One evening, Lopa and Kritika sit facing each other. Lopa's shadow falls to Kritika's right. Which direction is Kritika facing?
steps: In the evening, the sun is in the West, so shadows fall towards the East.
If your right is East, you face North.

varieties.name: Relative position of points
varieties.how: Put one point at (0, 0). Place every other point using the given distances (North up, East right). Read the asked position from the coordinates.

example.q: D is 60 m south of E. F is 40 m south of B. A is 30 m north of E. F is 50 m east of A. C is 50 m west of B. Where is C with respect to A?
steps: F is 50 m east of A: F = (50, 30). B is 40 m north of F: B = (50, 70).
C is 50 m west of B: C = (0, 70).
C is straight above A by 70 − 30 = 40 m.

tips: Draw the path with North up as you read the question.
For many turns, add clockwise turns and subtract anticlockwise turns, then turn once.
Learn the triples 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and 20-21-29; most distance answers use them.
Facing South, right is West and left is East; do not use your own left and right on the page.
In the morning, shadows fall West; in the evening, they fall East.
Read the last line twice: "direction of A from B" is the opposite of "B from A".
traps: Taking left and right as fixed on the page instead of relative to where the person faces.
Adding distances along the path instead of using net movement and Pythagoras.
Giving the reverse direction (the start from the end point instead of the end point from the start).
The back door of a north-facing house opens to the South.

questions.q: Ravi is facing North. He turns 90° clockwise and then 180° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
A man walks 3 km towards North and then 4 km towards East. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.solution:
The two moves are at right angles.
Distance = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km.

questions.q: Sita walks 10 m towards South. She turns left and walks 6 m, then turns left and walks 18 m, and then turns right and walks 9 m. How far and in which direction is she from her starting point?
questions.solution:
South 10 m: (0, −10).
Facing South, left = East: 6 m → (6, −10).
Facing East, left = North: 18 m → (6, 8).
Facing North, right = East: 9 m → (15, 8).
Distance = √(15² + 8²) = √289 = 17 m, towards North-East.

questions.q: Study the figure. A person walks from P to Q (5 km East) and then from Q to R (12 km North). What is the shortest distance between P and R, and in which direction is R from P?
questions.solution:
Net movement: 5 km East and 12 km North.
PR = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km.
R is up and to the right of P, so R is North-East of P.

questions.q: One morning after sunrise, Rahul was standing facing a pole. The shadow of the pole fell exactly to his right. Which direction was Rahul facing?
questions.solution:
In the morning the sun is in the East, so shadows fall towards the West.
The shadow is on Rahul's right, so his right side is West.
A person whose right is West is facing South.

questions.q: Point A is 8 m West of point B. Point C is 12 m North of B. Point D is 8 m East of C. What is the distance between A and D, and in which direction is D from A?
questions.solution:
Take B = (0, 0). Then A = (−8, 0), C = (0, 12), D = (8, 12).
From A to D: 16 m East and 12 m North.
AD = √(16² + 12²) = √400 = 20 m, towards North-East.
